title: Simplicity As Strategy
hook: Being able to juggle a complicated business is not a good reason to build one.
statement: The simplest path that scales usually beats the cleverest complicated plan.
explainer: Smart founders build complicated things because they can. Custom offers, five audiences, messy ops. You might handle it, but a business that needs you to be a hero every day won't scale.
sop: Sketch the simplest version of your business model.
Cut extra steps, offers, and dependencies.
Choose repeatable actions over clever custom work.
Score Simplicity, Repeatability, and Profitability from 1 to 10.
Add complexity only when it clearly boosts profit or quality.
equation_example: Simplicity 8, Repeatability 7, Profitability 6. 8 × 7 × 6 = 336 Strategic Power, out of 1,000. Higher means the model runs without heroics. Lower means it survives only because you personally hold the complexity together.
question: Name one part of your business that's complicated only because you can handle it, then simplify it.
closing_statement: Protect simplicity like it's a moat.
caption:
